Hi Emily — great to hear SignalOps found the demo useful. Attaching a first-pass efficiency matrix and a one-page pilot scope (efficiency_matrix_v1.xlsx, pilot_scope_signalops.pdf). Key takeaways up front:

- Short-chat (avg 32 tokens): batching helps only at high concurrent QPS; KV/prefix cache gives ~10-18% token cost reduction for repeated prompts (chat history reuse). q8 quant yields ~22-30% CPU/GPU throughput gain but may introduce subtle token-level differences for rare tokens — recommended for high-volume non-critical scoring.
- Long-doc (avg 2k tokens): batching provides 12-25% savings depending on service-level TTI targets; prefix cache less effective unless documents have repetitive prefixes. q8 gives 25-40% cost improvement but increases risk of hallucination in certain instruction-following prompts; recommend AB testing against float16.
- Embedding batch jobs: batching + dedicated batch workers -> 40-55% unit cost reduction. Quantization impact is minimal for most embedding models (we recommend quantized variants primarily for generative workloads).

Pilot suggestion (6 weeks):
- Credits: $40k compute credits + $5k engineering hours credit (recommended).
- Scope: run two parallel experiments: (A) chat app baseline (float16) vs q8 variant w/ KV cache enabled; (B) nightly embedding pipeline with batching + scale-out pool.
- Metrics: per-token cost, 95th percentile TTI, rouge/semantic-sim similarity on 200 eval prompts, error rates.

I've left operational notes and a recommended rollout timeline in the XLSX. Marcus and Lauren, can you confirm technical caveats and commercial fit?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes to surface for the pilot:

- q8 variants: our q8 kernels are stable for most causal and encoder-decoder architectures we ship, but we recommend locking generation temperature and top-p ranges for initial A/B to reduce variance.
- KV cache: prefix caching yields the best win when conversation turns are <40 tokens and there's high identity reuse (same user/system prompts). For long-doc workflows, consider chunked KV reuse with overlap to preserve context — this changes the cache hit profile and needs warm-up runs.
- Batching: continuous batching requires tuned batching delays; we recommend simulating production QPS on a staging pool to pick the delay that gives acceptable p50 vs cost.
- Quality regression gating: include automatic turned-on checks (semantic-sim threshold, hallucination heuristic) and a rollback policy.

Connor, I'll need one hour of your time Monday to sync on the staging config and a script to replay SignalOps traces.
